Oregon Data Centers

This is a great, yet depressing as fuck, column by Jackson Hoeke who writes for Oregon’s Bay Area on Facebook. They also post on Substack (link below). Little known fact, Cliff Bentz is currently sponsoring a bill to take ownership of the land around Crow Creek Reservoir in the Mt. Hood National Forest so the dam can be raised and the water used for the Google Data Center in The Dalles.
Oregon has paused the tax breaks for data centers but they need to do more regulating and halt new builds and expansions. Even PG&E finally acknowledged that data centers are costing residents, so they proposed a 29% rate hike for large data centers in Oregon to cover the infrastructure costs associated with their heavy energy use. Yet residential customers will only see a tiny 1.3% rate.

facts: On Oct. 28, 2026 (Tuesday), Washington County commissioners voted 3-1 to say the board does not currently support large-scale standalone data centers in unincorporated Washington County, without adopting a moratorium.

The resolution limits county-owned property sales, leases, NDAs and voluntary easements for known large-scale standalone data centers, and does not support job-creation tax incentives for data centers.
County staff told the board in September there are no known large-scale standalone data centers or applications in unincorporated Washington County.
On Oct. 12, the Forest Grove City Council voted unanimously to stop accepting and approving new data center applications for 120 days.
Gov. Tina Kotek on Oct. 9 ordered Oregon DEQ to pause air and water pollution permits for new or expanded data centers until July 1, 2027.
Washington County District 4 runoff pits former Hillsboro mayor Steve Callaway against Hillsboro City Council member Kimberlee Sinclair.
Callaway said he supports the current voluntary statewide pause on data centers and that state-level discussions on incentives and farmland protection are needed during it.
Sinclair cancelled her KGW interview due to unexpected circumstances and sent a written statement instead.
Washington County has become a hot spot in the debate over data centers, according to KGW.
Lawsuit filed in June challenges 17 enterprise zone tax exemptions approved for data center projects in Hillsboro and Washington County
